behaviorReferences.DEL-04: Retained PR identity is read from local synthetic Bitbucket at cancelled queueing and admission; closed, foreign, moved or unmarked PRs refuse continuation. Publication acquisition remains N5.3b2.

behaviorReferences.LIF-04: Actual controller SIGKILL leaves a live checked fetch child; the next owner stops verified old ownership before a fresh request. Cancelled RPC waiters do not orphan driven work.
behaviorReferences.SEC-02: Native target refs have UUID namespaces, final store/lifecycle authorization and fixed synthetic credential callbacks. No real credentials, provider or model access.
behaviorReferences.cancel-continuation: Actual managed cancelled work retains branch/path only after fresh configured PR verification at queue and again at admission.
behaviorReferences.target_refresh: Per-run admission order, strict normalized operator decisions, historical replay before provider access, live moved-target preservation, operator-held recovery, stopped pending fetches and shutdown drain.

auditCorrections: Each operation is registered before await and driven independently of its RPC waiter. A run epoch fences previously admitted work; Stop closes current checked Git and drains pending jobs. Global close fences all admission, and unverified cleanup remains visible on repetition.

Ordered target operations register a completion chain before spawning. Transport directories separately serialize one PublicationGit owner. The wrapper reuses its original lifecycle ticket for inner fetches so a stopped parent cannot obtain a newer epoch.

Canonical configured paths and serialized repository identity are retained separately from normalized Bitbucket client fields. Hosted check policy rejects unknown keys, duplicate names, oversized lists and invalid Unicode lengths.

Read-only Repository callbacks hold weak remote references and do not reacquire Repository operation locks. Cancelled-source PR verification checks exact marker, open state, branches, repositories and source head, then rechecks the durable receipt.

A fresh target fetch has a request-owned ref and a synchronous final guard over current control, candidate, ownership and prior request admission. A replay resolves the stored receipt before reaching transport.

Ordinary candidate association now includes the target-refresh coordinator notice in the same SQLite transaction. Startup retries only recorded recovery, never a new fetch; unresolved nonterminal recovery requires attention.
Shared target fixtures run extra remote-process verification before deleting their files. Fallback cleanup does not turn a surviving child into a passing teardown.
limitations: This accepts N5.3b1 native remote/target service libraries. Complete N5.3b2 publication intent/readiness/feedback delivery and N3.3b supervision before native workflow admission.
